speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
In pre-war times
the Department of Marine had an item in the Estimates each year for new construction and maintenance of lighthouses, sometimes as high as $1,000,000. I do not think that I shall be divulging a iState secret when I say that I had a very much larger amount than $400,000 provided for this year, but 1 was not able to persuade my colleagues to see the matter in the same light that I did, and I was asked to keep the amount down to $400,000. While I regret that, I am in hearty accord with the other members of the Government in accepting the principle that- our ordinary expenditures must be in keeping with our ordinary revenue. While I would like to do more, we really have not the money, and we must cut the coat according to the cloth.

I wish to emphasize what my hon. friend (Mr. Chisholm) has said; aids to navigation, whether on the St. Lawrence or in the Maritime Provinces or on the Pacific coast, should not be neglected. The minister's argument with regard to economy while it is not without some force, is not a sufficient reason why, if a lighthouse or range light is necessary at Grand Etang, it should not be put there. The minister said that he had proposed a much larger 135
-amount than $400,000 for lights and aids to Inavigatioii in his original Estimates, but [that Council did not accede to his request. Swell, it is quite evident that the Minister of 1 Marine has not as much pull with his colleagues as the Minister of the Interior (Mr. jMeighen) has, because, if my memory is -correct, the Minister of the Interior succeeded in getting his colleagues to agree to the appropriation of $100,000 more for parks in the West this year than was voted last year. It seems to me that there is more necessity for expenditure on lighthouses than there is for expenditure on parks in the West. It would be better if the Minister of the Interior would turn this $100,000 over to his colleague the Minister of Marine so that the life and property of people on both coasts of this country may be properly protected.

There is a great deal in
what the -hon. member (Mr. Duff) has just said. Complaints of this kind are being made by marine men not only in Nova Scotia, but also in Ontario. Considerable complaint has come from captains who are navigating on lake Erie with regard to the conditions at Erieau. Representations have been made to the department with regard to the danger to life and to vessels which are worth hundreds of thousands of dollars, but the reply has been that no accidents have taken place there, and that consequently there is no necessity for further action. While those who are thoroughly conversant with that section of the country and who know the difficulties that they have to contend with in making port with such valuable cargoes as go into Erieau state that further aids to navigation are necessary, hundreds of thousands of dollars are being spent in other departments upon works or enterprises which are not necessary. On stormy nights when heavy seas are rolling it would be a great comfort to those who are responsible for the navigation of vessels to know that they may enter harbour in safety. I hope that the minister will afford to the captains who are sailing on lake Erie, particularly those who go in and out of Erieau harbour, those facilities which can be provided at a cost of only a few hundred dollars and which would' ensure the safety of many lives and the protection of much valuable property.

I see by the Auditor General's report that this item also includes buoy service. We have a large number of very valuable buoys on the coasts of the Maritime Provinces on which the coun-



try has spent a great deal of money. Many of these are taken up and stored during the winter season and put out again in the following season. Last year we had numerous complaints from captains that most of the summer had passed before these buoys were put out. I hope that the same thing will not happen this year. I do not know why it happened; we have the equipment for the putting out of these buoys. There must be some lack of efficiency when they are not set out early in the spring so that vessels may have the advantage of them during the season when they are most needed.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: There is a great deal in what the hon. member says, but the department is very short of ships. The Earl Grey and the Minto, when we had them in that service, assisted in placing the buoys, as did the Aranmore, which, unfortunately, was wrecked last fall. The shortage of ships causes the delay, but we shall do the very best we can.
What ships have you in this service?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: The Stanley and the Lady Laurier. We hope that we may get the Aranmore off the place on which she is stranded so that she too may be available.
Will the minister say if any of the buoys have been put out this season yet?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
Certainly a very
large number but I am not prepared to state what the exact number is.

The inquiry of my
hon. friend has reference to larger buoys. I want to get some information respecting the smaller buoys that are taken up in the fall of the year when the ice makes along the coast. I would like to know ' if there is any scheme in operation as a result of which these buoys are placed by somebody. There are a great many points in my own county where the buoys were not placed until I looked after the matter myself. Now somebody ought to be in charge of this duty, but there appears to be nobody who is held responsible for placing the buoys. Will the minister tell me who is really responsible for placing these smaller buoys leading to the ports?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: Will my hon. friend state what particular port he has reference to?
I would say Margaree, for instance.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
That particular
port was under the Halifax agency until this year, but there has been a redistribution of the territory covered by the agencies, and it is now under the Charlottetown agency. I will write to the agent there and find out the cause of the delay that the hon. member refers to.

There is an officer
down there who lis responsible for the placing of these buoys. Why does not the department give him instruction to look after them in the fall and put them in place in the spring, all along this coast? Then there would he no trouble about the matter. There is a contractor, I understand, who is paid so much to do the work, but he does not take the responsibility, he receives no instructions until he reports to the department, or somebody does, that the buoys have not been placed. Then some official of the department will send instructions to him, but such a procedure involves delay, and may result in very disastrous consequences.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: The agent at Charlottetown has certainly been very remiss in his duties if what the hon. gentleman states is a fact.
It is true.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: I have no right to doubt what the hon. member states. The responsibility rests upon the agent at Charlottetown to see that all these buoys are placed, and if the work has not been done I must hold him responsible for the delay. I will see that a letter is promptly sent to him, and I will communicate a copy of the reply to my hon. friend, when I receive it.

What has been done
to repair the present South Bar lighthouse in the harbour of Sydney, which is a very important light? I understand the foundations were damaged a short time ago, and it is imperative they should be repaired and the lighthouse opened as speedily as possible.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: Doubtless the hon. gentleman is aware that the department has a lighthouse board that studies all these questiqns pertaining to the future need of new lighthouses. I will bring the matter to the attention of the board at their next meeting.

There has been a lighthouse on the South Bar for seventy, or perhaps one hundred years. A new light-

house was built a few years ago but the department thought it advisable to erect it further out at the point of the Bar than where the old lighthouse was. However, the foundations gave way, I suppose owing to the action of the sea, and the lightkeeper had to leave the new structure and make use of the old lighthouse. That must be very embarrassing to shipowners, or seamen, entering the port, and it is very desirable that the new lighthouse should be repaired and put in shape as speedily as possible.

I would ask how many
lighthouses there are on the Newfoundland coast the up-keep of which is paid by the Dominion Government as well as the salaries of the keepers.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: Seven is the number.
I understand the Dominion Government pays the cost of upkeep and the salaries of the keepers?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: Yes, we do.

I would call the minister's attention to a very important matter in connection with the condition of the lighthouses existing on that coast. The Cape Race lighthouse is perhaps one of the best, if not the best, on the North American continent. That lighthouse is of the utmost importance to navigators in both coming and going across the Atlantic. As the minister is well aware, for the last number of years-in fact ever since vessels have sailed the waters-there have been a great many wrecks either on the east side or on the west side of Cape Race lighthouse. Many steamers have been wrecked, and in some cases numerous lives have been lost. In conversation with a number of captains of steamers they made a suggestion to me which they asked me to bring to the attention of Parliament and the minister, and this is the suggestion: Just west of Cape Race, at the entrance of Trepessey Bay is Mistake point, and a little farther west is Cape Pine or )St. Shotts. If a powerful gas buoy with a groaner were placed about five or ten miles from the shore, half-way between those two capes, the steamers passing this area would either see the light or the gas buoy or hear the groaner, and know their position. It would be the means of saving a great many ships and a great many lives. As the minister knows, the shares of Cape Race are very rugged and precipitous and the water is very deep. Vessels cannot tell, by soundings exactly 135}	,
where they are until they place their jib-boom, or bow sometimes, up against the rocks. In bad or foggy weather when they are passing Cape Race it is difficult to tell their position, and the swift current there often takes them right onto the coast. The captains to whom I spoke suggested to me that it would be in the interest of shipping to have a large gas buoy at that point. Of course the providing of such an important aid to navigation at that point may be an international affair, and therefore the Newfoundland government might be asked to co-operate. Certainly the minister would be well justified in providing a sufficient amount of money to establish a gas buoy there as has been suggested. In view of the conditions which prevail there it is surprising that the suggestion was not made much earlier. Had it been carried into effect it would have been the means of saving many lives, and millions of dollars of property would not have been lost.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: The Canadian Government have never undertaken the responsibility of placing gas buoys along the Newfoundland coast. It is a matter that has engaged the attention of the Newfoundland government and which the Canadian Government have taken up with them from time to time. The subject is one to which 1 will with pleasure direct to the attention of the Newfoundland government. Every hon. gentleman will appreciate the fact that the Canadian Government could not properly maintain or look after a gas buoy so far distant from Canadian territory, and we have never, as I say, undertaken such a responsibility. However, there is a good deal in what the hon. member states, and I will again call the attention of the Newfoundland government to the matter.

I would like to get information in respect of the Lighthouse Board-its personnel, its location, its duties, dates of meeting, and so forth. If I can get this information on another item I shall not press for it now.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: The personnel of the board consists of the Deputy Minister of Marine, the chief engineer, a representative from the Shipping Federation, the Commissioner of Lights, and a representative from the Dominion Marine Association. They have no set dates for meeting, but they meet quite frequently whenever business demands it. Their duties relate to lighthouse needs.

When the minister again brings down these Estimates would he get me a report from the hoard as to what they have done in respect to the application for a range light at Grand Ma-tane? My people want this information, and I want it, and surely it is little enough for us to know what has been done, this matter having been before the board for three years or longer. What has the board done?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: I will be very glad to give that information.

I am not quite satisfied with the information given me in regard to the Bar light in Sydney harbour. I would like to know what the board intends to do about repairing that lighthouse, which was erected at a cost of $100,000 and is about to fall down. The matter is of great concern to the people of Sydney and North Sydney.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
I cannot make a definite promise, but I think in the very near future a new lighthouse will be built on the site of the one that was swept away.
Mr. McOOIiG: When can the captains navigating lake Erie waters expect any better light service than they are receiving at the present time at Erieau? A heavy revenue is derived at this port from the. valuable cargoes that are brought in there, and the very best lighthouse system should be provided, especially in view of the local dangers.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
We have a representative of the Lake Carriers Association on the Lighthouse Board, but at the moment I could not say whether he has made any representations in regard to the lighting system at this port. However, I will look into the matter and let the hon. member know.
Construction of lights and aids to navigations, including regulations of traffic in the Detroit river, and such other places as may be found necessary-$400,000.
What is meant by the regulation of traffic in the Detroit river?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: There is what might be called a dual control of traffic on the Detroit river: The Americans look after their part, and the Department of Marine look-after our part.

I am informed, it may be incorrectly, that the Department of Marine and Fisheries have certain gasoline boats on the Detroit river acting as revenue cut-

ters to prevent intoxicating liquor entering the United States. I would like to know whether that is true or not.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: The hon. member could not have been in the House when a similar question was asked 'by the hon. member for Lunenburg (Mr. Duff). I informed the latter gentleman that there was no foundation for the press report, and I make the same reply to my hon. friend.
What portion of this vote is used in regulating 'traffic on the Detroit river?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
About $5,000.
Signal service-$65,000.
The minister dismissed my question rather summarily in regard to iS't. Paul's island. I do not expect any information to-night, but when will the minister be able to give me that information?	,

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: I will be very glad to give the hon. member the fullest detailed information not later than two days from now, and possibly to-morrow.
What is the increase of $5,000 for?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
Salaries.
Administration of pilotage-$4'00,000.

I do not wish to take up the time of the committee, because I think it has been very well taken up tonight on individual matters, and I find from my experience that it is a great deal easier to get satisfaction by taking up these individual matters with the minister or the deputy minister rather than raising them on the floor of the House. I have always had very great consideration shown to me in connection with every matter that I have taken up with the department, and I have taken up many different matters. I wish to call the attention of the minister to the fact- that a very serious condition exists in the Bay of Fundy and the harbour of St. John, due to the unfortunate sinking of a pilot boat by a steamer coming up the bay. When I first applied to the department they with their usual promptness took the matter up at once and sent for the agent at St. John to discuss it with them. I would like to know if any definite arrangements have been arrived at. I know the department have for the last two or three years been considering the pilotage system in St. John arid the Bay of Fundy with a

view to putting it on a permanent basis similar to what they have established at Halifax and other ports. Pilot matters in St. John have been handled during the past number of years by a Board of Pilot Commissioners, some of whom were appointed by the Government, some by the city of St. John, and others by the Board o'f Trade of St. John. But they feel that the time has now arrived when the Government should take some definite action and take this matter of pilotage over entirely, and either supply the pilots with proper boats and equipment or else make some other suitable arrangements the Government may have in mind. I am bringing this matter to the attention of the minister, because I know the people, the Board of Trade and the shipping interests of >St. John, are very anxious to know what decision the Government have reached. If possible, I should like the minister to give me some information along those lines, and if he cannot give me it now, I should like to know when I may expect this information.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: I am happy to inform the hotn. member that all arrangements have been made, and the Marine Department will take over the pilotage service of St. John by the 15th May.

There is a very
large increase, namely, $200,000 in this item. It seems to me that the usual experience when the Government takes over anything is that it becomes more expensive. There is no reason why the ships should not pay for pilotage. (During the last few years shipowners have been making money, and it is a mistake that the Government should assume any expenditure in connection with pilotage, because all this pilotage service should be paid by the ships. I do not know what the plans of the minister jare or whether there is a contra account for this item or not. There may be one: but if so, iff would be well to have an explanation of it, because the item is a very large one, and I should like to lay down the principle that whatever is expended in pilotage on the coasts of this Dominion/ should be a tax on the shipping of the Dominion and not on the ordinary taxpayer.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
The hon. member
is quite correct. The pilotage dues will cover all the expenditure. This is merely a book-keeping entry, but the pilotage dues in each pilotage district throughout Canada fully cover the expenditure.
Does the minister estimate that the additional dues will amount to $200,000?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: Yes, and, I think, more.

The minister has given a
very short statement in reference to taking over the pilotage service at the port of St. John. Is this a special arrangement for St. John harbour, or is it general throughout the Dominion?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
The hon. member
will no doubt recall that at the last session of Parliament legislation was passed vesting the pilotage authority for the port of St, John as well as the other principal pilotage districts in the Governor in Council, and that really makes the Minister of Marine the pilotage authority. The system that the port o:f iSt. John will come under now is similar to what has been in force in the pilotage districts of Montreal and -Quebec for a long number of years. This does away entirely with the local pilotage board, and a local superintendent of pilots will be appointed at St. John, and' he will report to the General Superintendent of Pilots -at Ottawa. The pilotage districts that now c-orne under the Minister' of Marine are Halifax, (Sydney, St. John,. Montreal, Quebec, Vancouver and Victoria-.

If 'I understand the matter
correctly, pilots have in the past been licensed to do business, so to speak, on their own hook. Are these pilots who have been operating in the port of St. John to be kept on by the Government ,as Government appointees to do the work, or what will become of them?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
The department
will, of course, retain in the service the pilots Who are there now, and what ever pilot boats they have the department will have to take over and pay for. The only difference is that we are transferring the -authority of -the pilotage district o-f St. John from a local board to the Minister of Marine at Ottawa.
How does the income from pilotage dues compare with the expenditure of last year, throughout the Dominion?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
This is the first
season that all these pilotage districts apart from the -districts of Montreal and Quebec come under the Minister of Marine; but judging by our experience with those two districts, our revenue has been -somewhat greater than the expenditure.
Is the minister considering the matter of giving compensation to the owner of the pilot boat that was lost in the Bay of Fundy by being run down by a Canadian Government Merchant Marine boat?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: Certainly. Unfortunately there was a collision in the Bay of Fundy between a Canadian Government Merchant Marine ship called the "Canadian Voyageur'' and a pilot boat, but we shall have to negotiate with the pilots of St. John and see that they do not lose anything on account of the collision.
Is it accepted that the fault was that of the Government boat?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: An investigation will have to be held; I cannot know who will be held responsible for the collision until such time as the court of inquiry comes to a decision.

I thought the minister was committing his department a little too soon. It does not follow that because a smaller vessel collides with a larger one, the larger vessel was at fault. I am sure, if the pilot lost his vessel by reason of any faulty seamanship on the part of the captain of the larger vessel, the man should be recompensed, but' the facts will have to be ascertained first and the minister will decide on those facts. I notice the minister states that the pilotage district of the harbour of St. John is to be taken over on the 15th May. Does the same remark apply to the harbour of Sydney?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: No, the pilotage district of Sydney has not yet been formally taken over, and I cannot say just when it will be.
The season which is now under way will be carried on under the old system?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: Yes.

Do I understand the minister to say generally that the receipts from pilotage dues throughout the Dominion balance the expenditures? I find in the Auditor General's Report that $91,076.75 was expended in the administration of pilotage. I was endeavouring to lay down the principle that the expenditure in administering the pilotage should be in some way a tax on the shipping of the country, and I understood the minister to say that he was receiving more than he was spending as regards pilotage. Does
IMr. Ballantyne.]
that statement cover expenditures throughout the Dominion, or was the minister referring only to the river St. Lawrence and the harbour of St. John?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: We have not yet had one full season's experience with all the districts that I have mentioned, but as far as I can judge, we should come out on the right side. To take, for instance, the pilotage districts of Vancouver and Victoria from the 1st January to 31st March, the gross earnings amounted to $23,292.86 and the expenses were $20,505.49. I would not care to make too positive a statement, but my judgment is that in 1920 we ought to come out even, or very nearly so, if not a little on the right side.
The minister is not prepared to give a general statement for the whole Dominion showing the receipts and expenditures of each of the districts?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: I have not the figures here, but I know that 'the revenue does take care of the expenditure.
Will the financial year in this connection be the same as the Government financial year?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: Yes.

Whenever we hear of a business merger, we are told that overhead charges and administrative costs are to be cut down. The Minister of Marine is going to merge all the pilotage districts under one head in the Department of Marine. I presume that will result in a saving in the cost of administration. I would suggest to the minister that instead of having commissioners at each port he turn the work of the district over to the marine agents at the different ports-the marine agents a!t Halifax, Sydney, Vancouver and other places. In that way I think the Government would save a great deal of money.
I am sorry my hon. friend (Mr. Wig-more) has been delaying the Estimates of the minister, especially in view of the lecture which he read hon. gentlemen on this side of the House. He comes before the committee and asks if the owners of the "Canadian Voyageur" are going to pay for the pilot boat that was sunk in the Bay of Fundy, when he could get that information without any trouble by going to the Hunter Block and seeing the minister or his deputy. My hon, friend is not treating the committee or the minister right in bringing up a small matter like that

before the committee. I am surprised if the hon. membeT (Mr. Wigmore) has so much influence with the Department of Marine, that for a number of days or weeks there has been no pilot boat on the Bay of Fundy. If he has so much influence with the department he should have seen that the pilot boat was replaced within a day or two after the sinking. Apparently, he has not as much influence with the department as he thinks he has. Evidently some official of the department has been pulling his leg.
Pilot boats are not picked up every day.
Nor sunk every day.

As soon as the matter was called to the attention of the department they got busy at once and they have made arrangements along these lines. As to taking up different matters with the department, I think the time of this committee has been taken up with very simple matters that do not concern the ordinary member at all. These matters of detail concerning the different constituencies have take up the greater part of the time of this committee. They could have been dealt with more expeditiously by going to see the minister ot his deputy at his office.

If the hon. member i(s correct, then the statement I made a moment ago is also correct. If'it is not necessary for us to get up on the floor of this House and refer to matters affecting our constituents, why did my hon. friend get up on his feet and bring to the attention of the minister the fact that a pilot boat had been sunk in the Bay of Fundy and ask who was going to pay for the damages? I can tell my hon. friend that I am going to ask as many questions as I like, and I shall not allow him to tell me when to sit down.

I think my hon. friend (Mr. Wigmore) may be excused for bringing to the attention of the minister the matter he did, because it gave the minister ;an opportunity of making a statement which, I have no doubt, my hon. friend will be very glad to have go down to the people of St. John who are deeply interested in this matter. However, I am not concerned with * whether my hon. friend (Mr. Wigmore) thinks we are wasting time or not. I want to ask a few questions in regard to this pilotage business, as it is somewhat new to me. Are the pilotage arrangements which the minister has made for the port of St. John to be extended to the smaller ports
along the Bay of Fundy, or are they confined to that one port?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: St. John only.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
Before doing that
I desire to say, as Minister of Marine, and

speaking also for the Government, that it certainly is the privilege of hon. members in this committee to ask as many questions as they like. I have made no objection at all, and I should be very sorry to see the discussion cut too short, because hon. members and the public generally have the right to know how the money voted by this cotn-mittee is going to be spent, and if increases are being made, the reasons therefore.
With regard to hon. members, calling on the department over which I have the honour to preside, I think hon. gentlemen opposite will agree that I show them just as much attention and courtesy, and just as great a desire'to meet their wishes and requests, as I do hon. gentlemen on this side. I congratulate the constituency of Inverness in having such an'able and persistent representative in this House. I find no fault whatever with his coming to the department as often as he does, I know the particular case he has in mind, but the only reason I could not meet his views in that matter was again, the lack of money. It is, of course, the duty of myself and every one connected with the department to be courteous and to endeavour to meet the wishes of hon. gentlemen so far as we can.
In regard to the question, who shall be in charge of the pilots in the various districts, we are doing away altogether with the local pilotage hoards and we shall have a local superintendent in the different pilotage divisions. My only reason for bringing the pilotage authority under the Department of Marine was that there might be an increase in efficiency. I shall not go into details now, but I am thoroughly satisfied that the pilotage work will be much more efficient under the new system than it has been in the past. The expenditure may be somewhat greater under the new system, but if it is there will be a corresponding increase in the efficiency. There is no necessity for local commissioners because we shall have an experienced man who holds a master mariner's certificate as superintendent of pilotage for each district, and he will be under the general superintendent of pilots, Captain Robertson, who is located at headquarters.
These will be new appointees of the Government?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: Some of them, yes.
How long has this new system of pilotage under government control been in effect?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: That depends on the pilotage district you have in mind. The districts of Montreal and Quebec have been under the Minister of Marine for the past fifteen years. In fact, the deputy minister informs me that it is longer; they have been under the minister for at least twenty years.
I understand that it is the intention of the department to decrease the number of pilots between the city of Montreal and the city of Quebec.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: I am not aware of such an intention.
I received a communication to-day from a pilot informing me that the number of pilots between Montreal and Quebec was to be decreased from fifty to thirty-five.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
There is no such intention on the part of the department.
Maintenance and repairs to wharves-$10,000.
What wharves does this item refer to?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: This is a small vote for repairs that may be needed in connection with various wharves. We cannot tell what particular wharf or wharves will need repairs during the coming year, but I see that last year repairs were made in Nova Scotia amounting to $98.37; Prince Edward Island, $107.45; New Brunswick, $3,675.48; Quebec, $1,618.92; Montreal district, $198.82; Ontario, $1,714.04; British Columbia, $50; general account, $224.42; making an actual expenditure for last year of $7,687.50. We are asking for $2,000 less this year than the previous fiscal year, but we think it better to have a vote of $10,000, even though the expenditure last year was only $7,000 odd, in case the expenditures may amount to two or three thousand dollars more.

I want to draw the attention of thevminister to a certain matter, and I think I may be pardoned for so. doing if it may not be altogether within my purview. My hon. friend from St. John (Mr. Wig-more) has been largely devoting his attention to having the port of St. John properly attended to, and possibly he has not been able to find time to consider matters that are of some importance even though they may not 'be as important as the port of St. John. We have along the river of St. John-it is not in my constituency, but J come from the province-a large number

of wharves which were constructed many years ago iby -the Government of New Brunswick. A few years ago, I understand, an arrangement was made between the local and the Dominion Governments by which these local wharves were to be taken over by tihe Dominion Government, who were to be responsible for their repairs. 1 have not been up the river fox the last year or two, but I have been informed by a number of persons, and have received communications to the same effect, that these wharves are in a bad state of disrepair and that it is impossible for -steamers plying up and down the river to- tie up at the wharves. If the responsibility is upon the Dominion Government I would ask the minister whether a part of this money is to be used in repairing those wharves.

I want to inform my hon. friend that this matter does not come under the Minister of Marine at all. I may further inform the hon. gentleman that I have already taken up the matter with the Department of Public Works, which has charge of these wharves, and while things are not moving as -quickly as some of us may desire, I can assure my hon. friend that -the Acting Minister of Public Works and his officials are looking after the matter.

I am much obliged to my hon. friend for this information, but I should like to have a statement from the minister himself. If my hon. friend has been so successful, and with such quick dispatch has been able to have -matters attended to promptly by the Department of Marine, as he said just now, he might transfer the matter of these -wharves to that department and perhaps he would receive more expeditious service. Evidently the- information he has received from the Department of Public Works is not v?ry reassuring.

Oh, yes.
Mr. -COPP: The matter is not -one of concern to -my -particular constituency, but it appertains to the province from which I come, and I have had communications concerning it. I therefore thought that I would take this opportunity to call the attention of the minister to th-e condition of the wharves in question.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
I think the hon.
member is aware that the -construction of wharves comes under the Department of Public Works.
This is a matter of repairs.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
A -certain number
of these wharves were transferred to the Marine Department, and the amount I am asking is for maintenance in a small way to keep in a proper state of repair those wharves that are under the jurisdiction of the Marine Department.
Where are these wharves?"

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: I can give the expenditure by provinces, but I cannot tell where each wharf is located.

I ask this -question because there a number of wharves which I know are in bad condition. I do not bla-me the minister at all, and perhaps it might be well to leave the matter until his colleague has his Estimates before the -committee. I want to be sure, however, who is responsible for the matter.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: A few wharves may have been transferred to the Department of Marine but generally speaking they are under the Department of Public Works.

When the Estimates of
the Department of Public Works comes before the House, will there be a responsible head for that department or will the condition he the same as it is to-day?
Mr. BALLANTYN-E:	There will be a
lesponsible acting head in the person of the hon. Minister of Railways (Mr. J D Reid).
What becomes of the revenues accruing from these wharves?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: A certain percentage goes to the wharfinger, and the balance to the department.

For many years I have been bringing to the notice of the minister and his predecessor certain conditions with regard to two wharves in my county which I regard as part of the national railway system. One of them is right beside the railway at Grand Narrows. At that point passengers and freight coming by the railway are transferred to a boat that crosses the lakes over to a main body of Victoria county. It would be impossible for the railway to do business in tjiat section of the county without this wharf; the tracks run out upon it and the goods are transferred from the car to the ferry. I do not think any wharfage fees are collected alongside the railway. But for the landing of freight and passengers at Baddeck on the other side of the lake it was also necessary to build a public wharf. For many

years, while it was under the Public Works Department no fees wrere charged on the Baddeck wharf. These charges are small, but they are very bothersome, and I do think that as these two wharves are really part of the national railway system and absolutely essential to the operation of the road in that part of the country, no fees should be charged in connection with the handling of passengers and freight upon them. One of the reasons given last year for continuing these charges was that there was a wharfinger at Baddeck and that in order to pay him something would have to be charged. Well, the poor wharfinger is dead, and I do not think it is necessary to appoint any one in his place. The agents there look after the wharf, they are good, capable, honest men and they see that it is properly cared for.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
At present there
is no wharfinger at either of these wharves and no dues are being collected. But under the statute we are obliged, I am afraid, to appoint wharfingers as soon as possible and prescribe the required tariff.
To provide for breaking: ice in Thunder Bay, Lake Superior and other points deemed advisable for the good of navigation-$40,000.

During last winter the weather was very' severe and the harbour of Guysborough was frozen over for five or six weeks. Application was made to the department to have the ice broken and the department did all they could, but there was no suitable boat on the coast to do the work. I think it will be quite possible to have a boat so equipped that it could break ice in these harbours in case of emergency and also perform the ordinary service carried on by the department every year. I would like the minister to look into that matter and see if anything can be done. We are badly in need of an icebreaker at certain seasons on the coasts of the Maritime Provinces.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: The Stanley will be available as soon as the necessary repairs have been made, and when the new icebreaker is built it is the intention of my department to place the Montcalm down there. A considerable amount of icebreaking is required to be done on the coast of Nova Scotia every year, and I think the Stanley and the Montcalm will be able to cope with the situation,

May I, then, repeat a request I made to the minister on a previous occasion as respects the ports on the south-
[Mr. McKenzie. 1
ern coast of Nova Scotia? The minister helped us last year to the extent of his equipment, but he has not the proper equipment, and until he gets some additional boats he really cannot give us all the assistance we require.
To provide for telephones at different points throughout the Dominion in connection with aids to navigation-$500.

I want to make application to the minister-I made a similar application to the department last year-for a cable to Margaree Island. This is a very important island, where the fishing industry is carried on on a large scale. It is about two miles and a half from the shore. There is a tri-weekly mail service from the mainland to the island, and it is very important that this cable be supplied if that can be done at reasonable cost. I would like the minister to consider the matter, because I think it is very important.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
I will be very glad to consider it.
Amount required to pay Messrs. Job Bros, for the use of their wharf at Greenly Island- $375.
Is that a private wharf?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
Yes, the wharf is
owned by Job Bros., and we have to pay them this amount for the use of that wharf.

This appears to be a new
item. Nothing was paid last year.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: It appears that the Government have been using this wharf for the past twenty-five years, and have never paid anything for it. Job Bros, made a claim on the department, and the sum of $375 has been agreed upon as the amount which should be paid. It covers a period of a quarter of a century.

For what purpose is
the wharf used?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: For the purpose of unloading coal, lumber and provisions.

It appears that this
man has the patience of his ancestor. Is he the only Job now living? Where does he reside? The minister steered clear of telling us where he is.
Job Bros, are a well-known commercial firm in Newfoundland. Are they the parties mentioned here ?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
They are the only
Jobs that we know.

tMr. DUFF: How much money was paid last year in gratuities, or gifts, to the crews of vessels for saving life on the high seas? Sometimes instead of gratuities the gifts consist of gold watches or binoculars.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
If the hon. member will be good enough to bring the matter up again when we take up the Naval Estimates, under which the vote for life-saving equipment and stations comes, I will be glad to give him the information.
Meteorological Service, including Magnetic Observatory grants of $500 each to Kingston and Montreal Observatories, also allowance of $400 to L. F. Gorman, observer at Ottawa- $245,000.
There is a large increase in this item.

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
I wish to explain
the reason of the increase of $34,120. Part of it is for the augmentation of salaries, but the principal amount is for the opening up of a station at Winnipeg in connection with the Winnipeg Grain Exchange so that the weather conditions may be set forth throughout the Prairie Provinces. This will be most valuable information to the grain growers.
Is it contemplated to increase the salaries of the officers along the coast in connection with the meteorological station who have to do with the weather reports?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
No, it is not intended to increase the salaries generally.
Steamboat inspection-$105,470.
What is the object of the increase in this item?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: To increase salaries and appoint a few additional inspectors.
Where are these additional inspectors to be appointed?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
There is to be an
additional man in the province of Ontario, one in British Columbia perhaps, and one at Quebec.
Who is the inspector in Nova Scotia?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
Mr. Norman Curry.
Mr. 'CHISHOLM: Where is he located?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: Halifax.

Is he the only
inspector in the province of Nova Scotia?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: No, there is another inspector named D. J. Murray.
Is he also at Halifax?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: Yes.
Does the duty devolve upon these men of inspecting vessels in all parts of Nova Scotia?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext: Yes.
Who has been inspecting in the yard of the Nova Scotia Steel Company?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
We have the following inspectors in the province of Nova Scotia:	N. A. Curry, D. K. O'Brien, A.
McDomga.ll, D. J. Stevens, and D. J. Murray.
Mr. .T. H. (SINCLAIR:	Where are they
located?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
At Halifax.
Mr. J. H. 'SINCLAIR:	Which inspector
inspects the ships built by the Nova Scotia Steel Company in Trenton, N. S. ?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
It would be one
o-f the five, but which particular one inspects the Nova Scotia Steel Company's plant I am unable to say.
Is one of these officers present all the time while a ship is being built?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service

speechtext:
Does the minister receive reports from these inspectors regularly?
'Mr. BALLANTYNE:	Mr. Macdonald,
Chairman of the Inspecting Board, receives reports regularly.
Mr. J. H. 'SINCLAIR: Are those reports in the department?

speakerposition: Minister of Marine and Fisheries; Minister of the Naval Service
speechtext:
Yes.
Progress reported.
